description:
## Problem

Wrenflow runs Parakeet TDT via ONNX Runtime on CPU. On Apple Silicon, the Neural Engine (ANE) can run the same model ~5-10x faster through CoreML. For a 15-second recording, this means ~50ms inference instead of ~500ms — critical for both batch and streaming transcription.

## Current Architecture

- `parakeet_rs` crate wraps ONNX Runtime with `load-dynamic` feature
- ONNX Runtime dylib downloaded by `scripts/download-ort.sh`
- Model: `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-onnx` from HuggingFace (ONNX format)
- Runs on CPU execution provider only

## Options

### Option A: ONNX Runtime CoreML Execution Provider

The `ort` Rust crate supports CoreML EP. This would be the lowest-effort path:
- Add `coreml` feature to `ort` dependency
- Configure session to prefer CoreML EP
- ONNX Runtime handles the CoreML compilation internally
- May need the CoreML-optimized ONNX model variant

**Pros**: Minimal code changes, stays in Rust
**Cons**: CoreML EP has operator coverage gaps, may fall back to CPU for unsupported ops. Performance may be suboptimal vs native CoreML (extra ONNX→CoreML translation layer).

### Option B: Native CoreML via Swift

Use CoreML models directly from FluidInference (`parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-coreml` on HuggingFace):
- Download `.mlmodelc` (compiled CoreML model) instead of ONNX
- Write Swift wrapper that loads model, runs inference, returns text
- Bridge to Rust via existing UniFFI/FFI layer
- Can pin compute units: encoder → ANE, other components → CPU/GPU

**Pros**: Best possible performance, full ANE utilization, palettized weights support
**Cons**: macOS-only code path, significant new Swift code, dual model management

### Option C: FluidAudio Swift Package

FluidAudio is an open-source Swift package with CoreML Parakeet TDT support, including batch and streaming ASR:
- Add as Swift Package dependency
- Replace Rust `parakeet_rs` with Swift `FluidAudioEngine` for macOS
- Keep ONNX path as fallback for Linux/Windows

**Pros**: Maintained library, includes VAD and streaming support, ~110x RTF on M4 Pro
**Cons**: Swift-only (need to bridge back to Rust pipeline), dependency on third-party package

## Recommended Approach

Start with **Option A** (ONNX CoreML EP) for quick wins, then evaluate **Option B or C** if CoreML EP performance is insufficient.

For any option, the model download/management in `model_downloader.rs` needs to handle CoreML model variants alongside ONNX.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Inference runs on ANE when available (verified via Instruments / powermetrics)
- Inference time for 15s audio < 100ms on M1+ hardware
- Graceful fallback to CPU if CoreML/ANE unavailable
- No regression in transcription quality (WER)
- Model download handles CoreML variant (separate from ONNX model)
title: CoreML/ANE backend for Parakeet TDT inference

description:
## Problem
Currently, hardware access (microphone listing, audio warm-up, screen capture) can be triggered before the user grants permission, causing unexpected system dialogs. The guard is in Swift (AppState.init), which is fragile and platform-specific.

## Solution
Implement a reactive permission system in Rust core so that:

1. **PlatformHost trait** already has `get_permission(kind) -> OsPermissionStatus` — use it
2. **AudioCapture**, **AppContextService** (screenshots), and pipeline operations check permission state before accessing hardware
3. Permission state changes are **observable** — when host grants permission, core automatically unlocks features; when revoked, core stops
4. This works across all platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android) — each platform implements PlatformHost

## Approach
- `AudioCapture::new(host: Arc<dyn PlatformHost>)` — receives host reference
- `list_input_devices()`, `warm_up()`, `start_recording()` return error if `host.get_permission(Microphone) != Granted`
- Consider reactive/declarative model: host pushes permission state changes, core subscribes and reacts
- May need `PermissionObserver` callback or channel-based notification

## Acceptance criteria
- Impossible to trigger system permission dialog from Rust code without explicit permission grant
- Works on all platforms via PlatformHost trait
- Existing Swift code simplified (remove manual permission guards from AppState)
title: Reactive permission gate in Rust core

description:
## Problem

Wrenflow sends the entire recorded audio buffer to Parakeet TDT, including silence at the beginning (before user starts speaking) and end (after user stops speaking but before releasing the hotkey). Parakeet TDT inference time scales linearly with audio length, so unnecessary silence wastes compute.

## Solution

Trim leading and trailing silence from the 16kHz buffer before calling `transcribe()`. The drain thread in `audio_capture.rs` already computes RMS energy per chunk — we can reuse similar logic to find the first/last non-silent sample.

## Implementation

In `core/wrenflow-core/src/audio_capture.rs` or as a preprocessing step in the transcription path:

1. After `stop_recording()` returns `RecordingResult` with `samples_16k`, apply silence trimming
2. Walk from the start to find first chunk where RMS > threshold (e.g., 0.005)
3. Walk from the end to find last chunk where RMS > threshold
4. Keep a small padding (~100ms / 1600 samples) on each side to avoid clipping speech onset/offset
5. Ensure the trimmed buffer still meets the 1-second minimum required by Parakeet (pad with zeros if needed)
6. Chunk size for RMS: ~20ms (320 samples at 16kHz) — matches the granularity already used for level metering

## Edge Cases

- User records only silence → return empty/skip transcription (already handled by minimum duration check in pipeline)
- Very short speech surrounded by long silence → trim aggressively, pad to 1s minimum
- Continuous speech with no silence → no trimming, pass through unchanged

## Acceptance Criteria

- Recordings with significant leading/trailing silence transcribe ~10-30% faster
- No audible clipping of speech onset or offset in transcription results
- Trimming adds negligible overhead (<1ms for typical buffer sizes)
title: Trim silence from audio edges before transcription

description:
## Problem

Currently wrenflow is batch-only: user holds hotkey → records → releases → waits for transcription → text is pasted. The entire transcription latency is perceived as "dead time" after releasing the key. For a 5-second recording on CPU, this can be 500ms-1s+ of waiting.

## Solution

Run incremental transcription while the user is still recording. Text appears in the recording overlay in real-time. When the user releases the hotkey, most (or all) of the text is already confirmed, so paste happens almost instantly.

## Core Algorithm: Speculative Word Confirmation

Parakeet TDT produces stable output because it's a single-pass TDT model (no autoregressive decoder). This makes it ideal for a confirmation-based streaming approach:

### Inference Loop

While recording, every ~300-500ms:
1. Take the current accumulated 16kHz audio buffer
2. Run Parakeet TDT inference on the entire buffer (single forward pass)
3. Get word-level output with timestamps
4. Compare against previous inference results using the confirmation algorithm
5. Send confirmed + hypothesis words to the UI

### Word Confirmation

Maintain `historical_words: Vec<Vec<WordTiming>>` — results of last N inference runs (N=3-5).

For each new result:
1. Find the **longest common prefix** between current words and the longest historical entry (compare by normalized word text)
2. If common prefix length >= `min_common_prefix_count` (1-2 for TDT): words in prefix are **confirmation candidates**
3. Words appearing consistently across `token_confirmations_needed` runs (1-2 for TDT) become **confirmed**
4. Remaining words are **hypothesis** (may change on next run)

### Punctuation Rule

Don't confirm mid-sentence fragments. Only confirm up to the last sentence boundary (`.` `?` `!`) that is NOT at the very end of the output. This prevents locking in "I went to the" when the model might rephrase to "I went to see" on the next pass.

### Orphaned Word Recovery

If a word appeared in run N but disappears in run N+1 (no temporal overlap with any current word), collect it as "orphaned." Prepend orphaned words to the next confirmed output to prevent text from vanishing during streaming.

### Buffer Management

After confirming words:
- Trim the confirmed audio portion from the buffer (using confirmed words' end timestamps)
- Keep unconfirmed audio for re-processing in the next iteration
- This keeps the buffer size bounded and inference fast

### On Hotkey Release (Finalization)

1. Run one final inference on the remaining unconfirmed buffer
2. Confirm all remaining words (force-confirm, no prefix check needed)
3. Concatenate with previously confirmed words
4. Paste the complete transcript

## Architecture Changes

### Rust Core

**New module**: `core/wrenflow-core/src/streaming_transcription.rs`

```
StreamingTranscriber {
    model: &ParakeetTDT,
    config: StreamingConfig,
    
    // Buffers
    audio_buffer: Vec<f32>,           // accumulated 16kHz samples
    
    // Confirmation state
    confirmed_words: Vec<WordTiming>,
    hypothesis_words: Vec<WordTiming>,
    historical_words: Vec<Vec<WordTiming>>,  // last N results
    orphaned_words: Vec<WordTiming>,
    previous_result: Vec<WordTiming>,
    
    // Timing
    last_confirmed_time: f64,
    total_confirmed_time: f64,
}
```

**StreamingConfig**:
```
StreamingConfig {
    transcribe_interval_ms: u32,        // 300-500ms
    min_common_prefix_count: usize,     // 1-2 for TDT
    token_confirmations_needed: usize,  // 1-2 for TDT
    use_punctuation_rule: bool,         // true for dictation
    max_buffer_duration_s: f32,         // 15-30s
    max_historical_entries: usize,      // 3-5
    silence_threshold: f32,             // 0.005-0.01 RMS
}
```

**Key methods**:
- `feed(&mut self, samples: &[f32])` — append audio from drain thread
- `should_process(&self) -> bool` — check interval + energy
- `process(&mut self) -> StreamingResult` — run inference + confirmation
- `finalize(&mut self) -> StreamingResult` — force-confirm all on hotkey release

### Pipeline Changes (`pipeline.rs`)

- `Recording` state gains intermediate transcription results
- New event: `OnStreamingUpdate { confirmed: String, hypothesis: String }`
- On hotkey release: if streaming was active, finalize instead of full re-transcribe

### UI: Recording Overlay

The native NSPanel recording overlay (`dev.gulya.wrenflow/overlay` platform channel) needs to display streaming text:

- Add a text area to the overlay panel
- **Confirmed text**: white/bright, stable
- **Hypothesis text**: dimmed/gray, may update
- Update via platform channel messages from Rust → Swift → NSPanel
- Text should auto-scroll as new words are confirmed

### Threading

- **Drain thread** (existing): continues accumulating audio, but now also feeds `StreamingTranscriber`
- **Inference thread** (new): runs the 300-500ms inference loop, must NOT block the drain thread
- Communication: drain thread pushes audio via channel, inference thread pulls and processes
- Confirmed/hypothesis words sent to Swift/Flutter via existing Rinf signal mechanism

### Energy-based Skip

Reuse RMS energy calculation from drain thread. If the accumulated buffer since last inference contains only silence (energy < threshold), skip the inference iteration. This saves battery and CPU during pauses in speech.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Parakeet TDT thread safety**: `parakeet_rs::ParakeetTDT` may not be `Send`. If so, inference must stay on the thread that created the model. Use a dedicated inference thread with a channel for audio input.
- **Inference blocking recording**: inference takes ~200-500ms on CPU. The drain thread must continue accumulating audio during inference. The SPSC ring buffer + separate inference thread handles this.
- **ONNX Runtime concurrent inference**: Verify that ONNX Runtime handles overlapping inference calls correctly, or serialize via the dedicated thread.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Text begins appearing in the recording overlay within ~500ms of starting to speak
- Confirmed words never change after appearing
- Hypothesis words update smoothly without jarring flicker
- On hotkey release, paste happens within ~100ms (most text already confirmed)
- No audio samples lost during streaming (drain thread unaffected by inference load)
- Silence periods don't trigger unnecessary inference runs
- Works correctly for recordings from 1s to 60s+

## Goal
Replace the Flutter/Riverpod/Rinf presentation layer with a Rust-native GPUI application while preserving recording, transcription, model management, history, menu-bar behavior, permissions, overlays, signing, and runtime invariants.

## Target direction
- GPUI plus an Apache-2.0 component library for the main UI.
- UI-independent Rust runtime with typed snapshots/channels instead of Rinf transport.
- AppKit/objc2 or a minimal Swift shell for NSStatusItem, activation policy, permissions, launch-at-login, and existing screenSaver-level overlays.
- Parallel GPUI app target until feature parity; no mixed Flutter/GPUI event loops in production.

## Success criteria
- No Dart, Flutter engine, Riverpod, Rinf bindings, CocoaPods, or Flutter build phases remain in the release app.
- Menu-bar lifecycle, dynamic dock visibility, global hotkey, paste, permissions, onboarding, settings, history, models, updates, native overlays, and quit behavior match the current product.
- ONNX Runtime is embedded and signed; Developer ID build and notarization pass.
- Runtime invariants and regression tests remain green.
- The first GPUI release is a documented clean break: no pre-GPUI data migration, backward-compatibility or rollback guarantee.

## Kill criteria
Stop or reconsider GPUI if the spike requires a long-lived framework fork for NSStatusItem, activation policy, TCC, or release packaging, or if accessible text input cannot meet product requirements.

title: Ship and validate the GPUI production release
description:
## Outcome
Ship the proven GPUI architecture as a supportable production macOS release, not merely a successful migration build.

## Product-line decision
The first GPUI release is a clean break. Pre-GPUI Flutter configuration, history, models, recordings and schemas are not imported or preserved. Compatibility is required only for fresh installs, current GPUI persistence formats and updates within the supported GPUI release line.

## Workstreams
1. Production installation, lifecycle, current-format data integrity, current-GPUI updates and recovery.
2. GPUI/AppKit visual, accessibility, display and performance hardening.
3. Crash diagnostics, update recovery, observability and operational readiness.
4. Reproducible release provenance, notarization, security, licensing and support policy.
5. Human validation on byte-identical candidates followed by a controlled beta and production go/no-go.

All child acceptance evidence must reference the same immutable candidate where applicable. Existing product-feature issues outside this epic remain independent.
acceptance_criteria: Close only when every blocking child is closed; the published DMG is byte-identical to the candidate used for M01-M22 evidence; signing/notarization/provenance are retained; the declared macOS/hardware matrix passes; clean-account TCC and real VoiceOver acceptance pass; performance/power/memory budgets pass; fresh install, current-format persistence and corruption recovery, supported GPUI-line update recovery, crash recovery, uninstall and login-item behavior pass; beta exit criteria are met; and the release runbook names owners, stop conditions and recovery procedures. No pre-GPUI import, backward-compatibility or downgrade/rollback proof is required. No source inspection, ad-hoc signature or developer account substitutes for external acceptance.

close_reason: Added prewarm dummy inference in initialize() after model load — 1s silence transcription forces ONNX graph compilation upfront
description:
## Problem

First transcription after app launch is noticeably slower than subsequent ones. ONNX Runtime lazily compiles the compute graph on first inference call, adding ~1-3s of latency that the user perceives as sluggishness.

## Solution

Run a dummy inference immediately after `LocalTranscriptionEngine::initialize()` completes. This forces ONNX Runtime to compile and optimize the graph ahead of time, so the first real transcription has zero cold-start penalty.

## Implementation

In `core/wrenflow-core/src/transcription_local.rs`:

1. After `ParakeetTDT::new()` succeeds, generate 1 second of silence (16,000 zeros at 16kHz mono f32)
2. Call `model.transcribe_samples(silence, 16000, 1, None)` — discard the result
3. Log prewarm duration for diagnostics
4. This should happen on the background thread where model loading already runs, so it won't block the UI

## Acceptance Criteria

- First transcription after launch has the same latency as subsequent ones
- Prewarm adds no visible delay to app startup (runs async, model loading screen already shown)
- Prewarm duration logged at info level
title: Prewarm Parakeet TDT model on startup
